notes: Spare used in place of 20.8.4. The NCD cites the laser safety standard as 'ANSIZ1363' (ANSI Z136.3); vignettes say ANSI Z136.3.

criteria.text: Severe angina, CCS class III or IV (stable or unstable)
criteria.span: patients with severe (Canadian Cardiovascular Society classification Classes III or IV) angina (stable or unstable)

criteria.text: Refractory to standard medical therapy at maximum tolerated or maximum safe doses
criteria.span: which has been found refractory to standard medical therapy, including drug therapy at the maximum tolerated or maximum safe dosages

criteria.text: Angina from areas not amenable to PTCA, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass
criteria.span: the angina symptoms must be caused by areas of the heart not amenable to surgical therapies such as percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty, stenting, coronary atherectomy or coronary bypass

criteria.text: Laser use FDA approved for the purpose
criteria.span: Coverage is further limited to those uses of the laser used in performing the procedure which have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration for the purpose for which they are being used.
An ejection fraction of 25% or greater

criteria.text: Viable ischemic myocardium demonstrated by diagnostic study, not revascularizable by direct intervention
criteria.span: Have areas of viable ischemic myocardium (as demonstrated by diagnostic study) which are not capable of being revascularized by direct coronary intervention

criteria.text: Acute conditions stabilized or maximal efforts made to stabilize
criteria.span: Have been stabilized, or have had maximal efforts to stabilize acute conditions such as severe ventricular arrhythmias, decompensated congestive heart failure or acute myocardial infarction.

criteria.text: Trained physician; provider documents training of all ancillary personnel
criteria.span: Providers of this service must also document that all ancillary personnel, including physicians, nurses, operating room personnel and technicians, are trained in the procedure and the proper use of the equipment involved.

criteria.text: Provider has dedicated cardiac care units and meets ANSI laser safety standards
criteria.span: Coverage is further limited to providers which have dedicated cardiac care units

cases.note: CCS IV refractory to maximal therapy, diffuse non-revascularizable disease, EF 40%, PET viability, stable.
cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with CCS class IV stable angina despite maximally tolerated metoprolol, amlodipine, isosorbide mononitrate, and ranolazine. Angiography reviewed by interventional cardiology and cardiac surgery shows diffuse distal disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 40%. PET perfusion-metabolism imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the inferolateral wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. He has no arrhythmias, heart failure decompensation, or recent infarction. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.

cases.note: Boundary: EF exactly 25%; CCS III unstable angina (stable or unstable allowed) after stabilization.
cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with CCS class III angina that became unstable 3 weeks ago; she was hospitalized, treated, and has been clinically stable for 2 weeks on maximally tolerated antianginal therapy, but angina persists. Her LVEF is exactly 25% by echocardiography. Angiography shows diffuse small-vessel disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. Dobutamine stress echocardiography demonstrates viable ischemic myocardium in the anterior wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.

cases.note: Two prior CABGs with failed grafts, age 82, diabetes are not exclusions.
cases.vignette: 82-year-old man with diabetes and two prior coronary bypass operations, now with occluded grafts and native vessels unsuitable for further bypass, angioplasty, stenting, or atherectomy. He has CCS class IV angina despite maximum safe doses of beta blocker, nitrate, calcium channel blocker, and ranolazine. LVEF is 45%. Nuclear viability imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the lateral wall not capable of direct revascularization. He is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
